turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you, too. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't seem to get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. 

It feels like every time I have to go into town, every banker or county person is just staring right at the cracks, the spots, and the sagging skin. My wife keeps telling me I'm making a big deal out of nothing, that I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life. But I just can't stop focusing on it. It's really starting to bother me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an inability to stop focusing on perceived flaws in his face and hands (cracks, spots, sagging skin) that others, such as his wife, consider normal or slight.

turns.doctor_question: How certain are you that the cracks, spots, and sagging skin are as noticeable to other people as they seem to you?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I guess I'm not... I mean, I don't know for an absolute fact what's going through their heads. Like I said, my wife swears nobody is paying attention to it. But when I'm standing there across the counter from someone, it just feels like it's the very first thing they notice. 

I don't have any real proof they're staring right at the cracks or the sun spots, but... I just figure, if it looks this rough to me in the mirror, they have to be seeing it too. It's just hard to shake that feeling once I'm out in public.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes ongoing concern with perceived skin defects (cracks and sun spots) that others, such as his wife, do not notice, and notes it is hard to shake the feeling that others notice them in public.

turns.doctor_question: How often do you check your face or hands in a mirror because of these concerns?
turns.patient_response:
I check pretty often, I guess. Mostly when I have to go somewhere public. Like... before I leave for a loan meeting, or if we're setting up a craft-fair table, I'll keep checking the bathroom mirror before I head out. And then I'll get in the truck and check the truck mirror, too. 

I just sit there turning my hat this way and that, trying to see how the skin looks. And with my hands... I catch myself comparing them to the younger workers' hands all the time. Honestly, I do it until I realize I've just wasted good time I really should be using out on the farm.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes frequently checking his skin in the bathroom and truck mirrors and continually comparing his hands to younger workers, clearly indicating repetitive behaviors related to appearance concerns.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think it is possible that your face and hands look less noticeable to other people than they seem to you, or are you convinced they definitely look seriously flawed to them?
turns.patient_response: I don't know for sure. I guess... I guess it's possible it's not as noticeable to them as it is to me. My wife tells me that all the time, and I know she wouldn't lie to me. But I'm just not convinced. When I look in the mirror, it looks pretty bad to me, so it's hard to believe they aren't seeing the same thing. I'm not 100% certain, but it sure feels like they're looking right at it.

turns.doctor_question: When you are around other people, is your fear mainly that they will notice your skin, or do you worry about being judged for other reasons as well?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it's really just the skin. I mean... I don't sit there worrying about if they think I'm not smart or if I'm bad at my job or anything like that. I've been farming a long time, I know who I am and I'm comfortable with that part of myself. 

It's just... yeah, it's just the cracks and the sun spots. That's the only thing on my mind when I'm standing in front of somebody. I don't really have any other big worries about being judged, just how rough and old my face and hands look.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms a preoccupation with perceived appearance flaws, stating that cracks, sun spots, and how rough and old their face and hands look are the only things on their mind around others.

turns.doctor_question: When you check your face or hands, do you mainly do it to assess how flawed they look, or do you feel driven to check in order to prevent something bad from happening?
turns.patient_response:
I think it's mostly just to see how they look. I mean... I'm not checking because I think something bad is going to happen if I don't. It's not like that. 

I just... I get to worrying about how rough my skin is, and I want to see exactly how bad the spots and the cracks are that day. So I look just to assess the damage, I guess you could say. I'm not trying to prevent anything, I just can't stop checking to see how flawed it all looks.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent worry about skin roughness, spots, cracks, and perceived flaws, indicating preoccupation with appearance.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports an inability to stop repeatedly checking their skin and hands to assess perceived flaws.

turns.doctor_question: How much does worrying about your face and hands interfere with your daily activities or responsibilities?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it gets in the way a fair bit. I mean... I've actually missed calls with our bankers, and I've put off making some important farm decisions. I just couldn't get myself looking acceptable enough to go sit down in a room with people. 

And then... well, we also run a retreat and do craft sales, and I've completely stopped agreeing to be in any photos that would help promote that stuff. I just can't do it. So, yeah, it definitely interferes with my responsibilities more than I'd like to admit.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms significant preoccupation with their appearance, stating they avoid meetings and photos because they cannot get themselves looking acceptable enough.
